subject: Prompt v3: acceptance gates, embargo windows, and deconflict calendar
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt v3: acceptance gates, embargo windows, and deconflict calendar

Team —

Quick sync request. Product wants to push Prompt v3 (promptset changes + small rewrites) into the canary next week but engineering has flagged a resource conflict with the infra sprint. Before either side makes decisions, need to align on the acceptance gates so we can: 1) set a minimal staging soak, 2) decide a safe traffic canary, and 3) define explicit rollback triggers.

Proposed minimal asks from product/evals side:
- Acceptance metrics for A/B (promptset v2 -> v3): delta on intent accuracy F1 (absolute), helpfulness score (crowd eval), and safety false-positive delta.
- Safety ceilings: no >0.2% absolute increase in safety rejects; if safety fails fire immediate rollback.
- Quality floor: relative F1 drop <=0.8% over baseline across the provided prompt slices.
- Monitoring: 1) realtime alerting on safety + quality, 2) manual review queue for top 50 failures/day.

Engineering asks: we need explicit latency & memory SLOs we can gate on (P95 P99), plus a deconflict window for the autoscaler rollout.

Questions for this thread:
- Marissa / evals: can you confirm concrete metric formulas and one human-eval pass cutoff we can use for the 48-hour canary?
- Karthik / infra: what gating on latency is required to approve canary? and any rollout blackout windows?
- Soojin / CS: are there customer-facing embargo constraints (Nimbus Health) we need to respect?

I attached a skeleton schedule (we'll link the full sheet in the Drive). If we can't reach consensus by EOD Wednesday, product will push the canary but I'll ask for a 1% traffic cap and extended monitoring hold.

Thanks —
Ethan

--
Ethan Park

Subject: Re: Prompt v3: acceptance gates, embargo windows, and deconflict calendar

Ethan —

Thanks for pulling this together. I uploaded an evaluation matrix (eval_matrix_v2.csv) and sketched thresholds. High-level proposed acceptance gates (we should finalize numbers in the doc):

1) Quality delta gate (automated):
   - Intent F1 relative drop <= 0.8% across prioritized slices (billing, prescriptions, scheduling).
   - Helpfulness crowd score not below baseline mean -0.25 std.

2) Safety gate (blocking):
   - Safety label increase <= 0.1% absolute; any single-day increase >0.25% triggers immediate rollback and manual safety review.

3) Latency/infra (blocking for canary):
   - P95 generation latency delta <= +40ms (compared to baseline infra config)
   - Memory growth must be <8% on 8k token long running sessions.

4) Staging soak / canary plan:
   - Staging: 48h automated tests + 1000 human-eval pairs (we'll run the sample in staging_examples_20260827.jsonl).
   - Canary: 1% traffic for 72h with continuous monitoring and daily triage. If all gates pass, escalate to 10% -> 25% over 24h steps.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Provide the exact prompt variations (we need the templated variants so evals can include them).
- Add a feature flag tag and a rollback tag on the deployment (we can coordinate naming).

I'll be on the 10:30 sync if you want to walk the matrix.

Attachments: eval_matrix_v2.csv

—
Marissa Cole
Group Product Manager, Evals

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt v3: acceptance gates, embargo windows, and deconflict calendar

Quick technical notes from infra:

- Latency gating: we can gate on tail latencies but need specific metric definitions. I propose: generation P95 <= 200ms and P99 <= 450ms on the canary config (measured across 99th percentile token distribution we expect in production). If we see >10% increase on P99 we should pause rollout.

- Resource constraints: the promptset changes interact with KV cache hit patterns — expect a temporary 5-12% memory delta. We can pin quantization profile to limit memory, but that may move the latency numbers.

- Rollback mechanics: we support immediate rollback via feature-flagging + model-routing fallback. Please add a rollback tag in the deploy manifest (e.g., promptv3-rollback-202608) and a human on-call for first 6 hours of canary.

- Calendar deconflict: we have autoscaler maintenance scheduled Fri 28 Aug 02:00-04:00 UTC; suggest avoiding canary start in that window.

I'll sync with Marissa to confirm the exact prompt variant list.

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infra Engineer

Ethan / Marissa —

We noticed an uptick in hallucination-type responses in the staging environment this morning after the prompt v3 patch was applied. I pulled a few examples and attached the file (staging_examples_20260827.jsonl) — the two examples where the model invents a medication name are concerning for clinical workflows.

Requesting an immediate hold on any canary that uses this prompt variant until you can confirm the safety gating in your matrix covers these failure modes. Our legal/compliance team is on standby; given the customer-safety impact, we would prefer a longer staging soak and a mandatory human review on any medication/prescription related prompts.

Happy to hop on a call — we have clinical ops available through EOD Pacific.

Thanks,
Ravi
Principal Product, Nimbus Health
